status: Tiepolo's 1965 inventory (transcribed 2020) lists them as wholly in cipher; no decipherment noted, unlike the Costantinopoli items of the same inventory where 'decifrazione' is stated. Not on DECODE, no repo hit (known.py: Spinelli = only the Florentine Beinecke family). Letters received abroad in Venetian cipher were read by the resident with his own key, so the clear text may survive in the Senate's Deliberazioni (Secreta, Corti/Napoli) or the Capi's registers; the originals themselves are probably not interlined.
why: October 1618 is the height of Venice's quarrel with the viceroy Osuna and the aftermath of the 'Spanish conspiracy'; instructions sent to the Naples resident in full cipher were the most secret part of that correspondence.
score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 Venice archives sweep (research/venice_archives/); not viewed
verify: Order scans of Archivi propri ambasciatori, Napoli 7bis; compare with the Suriano-period residents' cipher (CX, Cifre chiavi e scontri di cifra, b. 1 fol. 3, key a = z10, used 1616-23) and look for the clear text in Senato, Deliberazioni, Secreta (Napoli) and Capi CX lettere, Oct 1618.
